title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence After at Most K Operations
summary: Given a string s and an integer k , find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence that can be obtained by performing at most k operations.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k , find the length of the longest palindromic subsequence that can be obtained by performing at most k operations. In one operation, you can replace any character in the string with the next or previous character in the alphabet, with wrapping around the alphabet (e.g., 'a' becomes 'b' or 'z', and 'z' becomes 'a' or 'y').
constraints: s has 1–200 lowercase letters and 1 <= k <= 200.
One operation moves one chosen character one alphabet step forward or backward, wrapping between a and z.
Return the longest palindromic subsequence obtainable with at most k operations.
hints: Matching two endpoint letters costs their shortest circular alphabet distance.
Memoize the best subsequence length for an interval and remaining budget.
Either skip the left endpoint, skip the right endpoint, or pay their match cost and take both when affordable.
Every palindromic subsequence makes one of these endpoint choices; memoization selects the longest feasible result over all choices.
editorial: Every palindromic subsequence makes one of these endpoint choices; memoization selects the longest feasible result over all choices.

Using wraparound changes makes the entire six-character string palindromic within the budget.
